synopsis: Ultrasonic remains a possible sensing option, not a confirmed component of the heavy off-road automatic braking system; the research therefore covers it alongside camera, radar, lidar and other options [f2035, f3678, f6625, f8257]. Expert opinion identifies low-speed near-field geometry and control logic as useful virtual-testing applications, but acoustic reflections, installation effects, weather and contamination still require physical correlation [f1742, f1743, f499]. The booklet rates ultrasonic simulation among its weakest-evidenced cases: it found no published simulation-versus-reality validation in rain, snow, wind, dust or mud, and the accessible 2024 road-sensor study did not establish performance across the requested heavy-off-road weather and soiling matrix [f4432, f4581, f4577, f12659]. Commercial acoustic stimulation is evidenced for automotive parking, but independent heavy-off-road HIL/VIL evidence was not found; Isaac Sim's ultrasonic implementation is a ray-cast range model rather than an acoustic model [f5321, f5322, f8548]. Planning should therefore treat ultrasonic simulation as low credibility until correlated with company measurements, obtain ultrasonic-specific range or echo recordings rather than rely on camera logs, and ensure test surrogates reproduce the relevant ultrasonic response [f7086, f7099, f5626, f84, f2556].
